Build a Simplicial Complex

Source: R/simplicial.R
build_simplicial.Rd

build_simplicial() builds a simplicial complex, the higher-order structure of a network: besides nodes (0-simplices) and edges (1-simplices) it holds filled triangles (2-simplices), tetrahedra and larger groups of nodes. Three constructions are available through type:

  • Clique complex ("clique"): every clique of the network whose edges reach threshold becomes a simplex, the standard bridge from a graph to algebraic topology.

  • Pathway complex ("pathway"): the states on each higher-order pathway of a net_hon, net_hypa or net_mogen (or of one built from a tna model or netobject) become a simplex.

  • Vietoris-Rips complex ("vr", alias "rips"): the input is a non-negative distance matrix, every group of nodes whose pairwise distances are all at most max_scale becomes a simplex, and each simplex records the scale at which it enters (its largest pairwise distance), so persistent_homology() can read the filtration.

A clique complex is fixed by the thresholded graph, since every clique is filled in; its Betti numbers count the holes that remain, such as cycles of edges that no triangles fill. Its shape depends on threshold, so read betti_numbers() at more than one threshold, or follow the features across all of them with persistent_homology(). A pathway complex is built from paths observed in the sequences, so its simplices say which states occur together on a path. simplicial_degree() and q_analysis() describe how the nodes take part in the complex.

Usage

build_simplicial(
  x,
  type = "clique",
  threshold = 0,
  max_dim = 10L,
  max_pathways = NULL,
  anomaly = c("all", "over", "under"),
  max_scale = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'simplicial_complex'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'simplicial_complex'
plot(x, combined = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

x

The network: a square weight matrix, a tna model, a netobject or cograph_network, or a net_hon, net_hypa or net_mogen. With type = "vr", the matrix holds non-negative distances. The clique and Vietoris-Rips constructions read the weight matrix of any of these networks; with type = "pathway", a bare cograph_network or a matrix raises an error. For the print() and plot() methods: a simplicial_complex object.

type

The construction: "clique" (default), "pathway" or "vr" (alias "rips", stored as "vr").

threshold

For type = "clique": the smallest absolute edge weight an edge needs to enter (edges at exactly threshold are included). Zero weights are never edges. Default 0. Ignored for "vr", which uses max_scale, and for "pathway".

max_dim

The highest simplex dimension built (a k-simplex has k + 1 nodes), a non-negative whole number. Default 10. When a larger clique is cut at this dimension, the clique or Vietoris-Rips complex is marked truncated; betti_numbers() then warns with class nestimate_truncated_complex, as does persistent_homology() on a Vietoris-Rips complex. A pathway with more than max_dim + 1 distinct states is cut to its faces of that size, without the truncated mark.

max_pathways

For type = "pathway", how many pathways to keep: the most frequent higher-order paths for a net_hon, the most frequent transitions of mogen_transitions() at the optimal order for a net_mogen (the highest order fitted when the optimal one is 0), and for a net_hypa the anomalous paths ranked by their observed / expected ratio (see anomaly). Default NULL (all).

anomaly

For type = "pathway" on a net_hypa: which anomalous paths become simplices: "all" (default), "over" or "under". Over-represented and "all" paths are ranked by the largest ratio, under-represented ones by the smallest. Possible paths that never occur are left out, since a pathway simplex is a set of states observed together on a path.

max_scale

For type = "vr": the largest distance at which an edge enters; longer edges are left out. Default NULL, the largest finite distance.

...

For type = "pathway" on a tna model or netobject: method ("hon", the default, "hypa" or "mogen") chooses the higher-order model built from it, and the other arguments go to build_hon(), build_hypa() or build_mogen(). For the print() and plot() methods: ignored.

combined

For the plot() method: TRUE (default) draws the four panels (f-vector, Betti numbers, simplicial degree per node and degree by dimension) as one 2 x 2 figure, which needs gridExtra; FALSE returns the four ggplots in a named list (f_vector, betti, degree, degree_heatmap) to print, save or arrange separately.

Value

A simplicial_complex object. print() shows the counts, the density, the f-vector (simplices per dimension), the Euler characteristic and the non-zero Betti numbers; plot() draws the f-vector, the Betti numbers and the simplicial degree of each node; betti_numbers(), euler_characteristic(), simplicial_degree(), q_analysis() and persistent_homology() read it. The object's fields:

simplices

List of integer vectors, one per simplex, each holding the sorted indices of the nodes it spans. Every face of every simplex is present, as are all 0-simplices (isolated nodes included).

nodes

Character vector of node labels, which simplices index.

n_nodes, n_simplices

Counts of nodes and simplices.

dimension

Highest simplex dimension present.

f_vector

Named integer vector dim_0, dim_1, ...: the number of simplices of each dimension.

density

n_simplices divided by the number of simplices a complete complex on n_nodes nodes would have up to dimension.

mean_dim

Mean simplex dimension.

type

"clique", "pathway" or "vr".

truncated

For the clique and Vietoris-Rips complexes: whether max_dim cut a larger clique.

A Vietoris-Rips complex also holds filtration (the scale at which each simplex enters, in the order of simplices) and max_scale (the cap used), which persistent_homology() reads.

The print() method returns its input invisibly. plot() returns the drawn grid grob invisibly with combined = TRUE, and the named list of four ggplots invisibly with combined = FALSE.

Details

For the clique and Vietoris-Rips complexes the weight matrix is made symmetric first (the larger absolute weight of the two directions for a clique complex, the larger distance for a Vietoris-Rips complex) and its diagonal is not read. Cliques are found with igraph::cliques() when igraph is installed, and by Bron-Kerbosch otherwise.

See also

betti_numbers, persistent_homology, simplicial_degree, q_analysis

Examples

mat <- matrix(c(0,.6,.5,.6,0,.4,.5,.4,0), 3, 3)
colnames(mat) <- rownames(mat) <- c("A","B","C")
sc <- build_simplicial(mat, threshold = 0.3)
print(sc)
#> Clique Complex 
#>   3 nodes, 7 simplices, dimension 2
#>   Density: 100.0%  |  Mean dim: 0.71  |  Euler: 1
#>   f-vector: (f0=3 f1=3 f2=1)
#>   Betti: b0=1
#>   Nodes: A, B, C 
betti_numbers(sc)
#> b0 b1 b2 
#>  1  0  0 

# Vietoris-Rips on a distance matrix:
d <- 1 - mat
diag(d) <- 0
sc_vr <- build_simplicial(d, type = "vr", max_scale = 0.6)
